title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics
by: Michael Armbrust, Ali Ghodsi, Reynold Xin and Matei Zaharia (Databricks, UC Berkeley, Stanford), CIDR 2021
summary: The paper that set out the lakehouse as an architecture. It argues that the two-tier setup of a data lake feeding a separate warehouse brings stale data, reliability problems, extra cost, lock-in and weak support for machine learning, and that warehouse features can instead sit on open formats such as Parquet and ORC: a transactional metadata layer like Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg, plus caching, auxiliary data and layout optimizations. It reports TPC-DS results from Databricks’ Delta Engine that compete with cloud warehouses; the authors work at Databricks, which sells this architecture.
